correctness.rationale: The stationary generator on x^p y^q has reset loss only for q>0. Normalizing time by r and position and driver by sqrt(D/r), I recovered the three forward moments by recursive symbolic evaluation (replay: python /workspace/branches/independent_moments.py, SymPy; output /workspace/branches/independent_moments.log). The exact fourth-moment cross difference is -2(b-c)(7bc+3b+3c-27). Its derivative and K-2=b(9-b)/((b+2)(b+3)) give precisely two positive preimages for 2<K<Kmax; the lower endpoint b=0 is excluded, K=2 occurs only at b=9, and the maximum has a single preimage. As an independent sign check, on distinct positive equal-K pairs write t=b+c; then 0<t<9 and both arguments satisfy x^2-t*x+(27-3*t)/7=0. Reduce the numerator and denominator of H to linear residues. The numerator of (H(b)-H(c))/(b-c), with the original positive denominator Q(b)Q(c), is 14256(t+5)^2(307760+63141t-290t^2-51t^3)/2401. Since 290t^2+51t^3<6741t, it is strictly positive. Thus the larger branch strictly increases H. A prescribed positive variance can be matched at either branch by adjusting s, so the ambiguity is real without m6. Once the branch is known, variance gives s; simultaneous rescaling of mu,r,D changes only the clock, not the stationary distribution. Neither statistical accuracy from samples nor separate recovery of all three rates is claimed.

value.rationale: For an established exactly solvable persistent-noise model, the result identifies where variance and kurtosis genuinely fail to distinguish a memory ratio, and which next consecutive even moment resolves it uniformly over admissible positive parameters. The global ordering is usable for choosing between two moment-matched parameter sets, not just a new parametrization of a tabulated moment. The result is about population observability, not practical estimator conditioning or absolute parameter recovery.
